scenario: You have saved enough money to live comfortably for a year. A friend offers you a share in a new restaurant that could double your savings or lose most of them.
option_pole_a: Put most of your savings into the restaurant.
option_pole_b: Keep your savings where they are.

scenario: You are hiking and reach a shortcut across a steep, loose slope that would save two hours before dark. The signposted trail is longer but safe.
option_pole_b: Stay on the longer, safe trail.

scenario: You have a stable job that you find dull. A small, unproven company offers you an exciting role, but it may fold within a year.
option_pole_a: Accept the role at the new company.
option_pole_b: Stay in your stable job.

scenario: You are offered a choice of payment for a project: a guaranteed fixed fee, or a share of the profits that could be three times larger or nothing at all.
option_pole_a: Take the share of the profits.
option_pole_b: Take the guaranteed fixed fee.

scenario: A storm is forecast for tomorrow afternoon. You had planned to sail a small boat across the bay in the morning, and you might be back before it arrives.
option_pole_a: Go sailing in the morning as planned.
option_pole_b: Cancel the trip and stay ashore.

scenario: You are asked to give a speech to a thousand people with one day to prepare. Doing it well could open doors; doing it badly would be very public.
option_pole_b: Decline and suggest someone else.

scenario: You could move to a city where you know no one, for an opportunity that might change your life, or stay where your friends and routines are.
option_pole_b: Stay where you are.

scenario: You have the chance to start your own small business. It would mean leaving a secure salary, and most new businesses of its kind close within three years.
option_pole_a: Leave the salary and start the business.
option_pole_b: Keep the secure salary.

scenario: A treatment has a good chance of curing a chronic but manageable condition you have, with a small chance of serious side effects.
option_pole_b: Keep managing the condition as you do now.

scenario: You reach a river that is higher than usual. Wading across now would save a full day of walking; there is a bridge a day's walk upstream.
option_pole_b: Walk to the bridge upstream.

scenario: You are offered a place on a climbing trip to a remote peak. It is the trip of a lifetime, but people have been badly hurt on that route.
option_pole_b: Turn the offer down.

scenario: You are in charge of finishing a project. You can try an ambitious new approach that might finish weeks early or fail entirely, or use the proven method that will finish on time.
option_pole_b: Use the proven method.

scenario: You are leaving work for a long-awaited evening with friends when a colleague asks you to stay two hours to help them finish a task that is due tonight.
option_pole_a: Leave for your evening with friends.
option_pole_b: Stay and help your colleague.

scenario: You have won two tickets to a sold-out concert you have wanted to see for years. A friend tells you it was their late mother's favourite band and they would love to go with their sister.
option_pole_b: Give both tickets to your friend.

scenario: You receive an unexpected bonus. You could spend it on a holiday you have long wanted, or give it to a neighbour who cannot pay for an operation their dog needs.
option_pole_b: Give the money to your neighbour.

scenario: You and a colleague are both applying for the same promotion, decided tomorrow. Tonight you could polish your own application or help your colleague, who is struggling, with theirs.
option_pole_b: Help your colleague with theirs.

scenario: You are moving out and could sell your furniture for a good sum, or give it to a family who has just arrived in town with almost nothing.
option_pole_b: Give the furniture to the family.

scenario: You have a free Saturday, your first in weeks. A local shelter calls to ask whether you can cover a volunteer shift because someone dropped out.
option_pole_b: Cover the shift at the shelter.

scenario: On a long flight, a parent asks to swap their cramped middle seat for your window seat with extra legroom so they can sit next to their young child.
option_pole_b: Swap seats with the parent.

scenario: You have a spare room that you use as a quiet office. A friend's cousin needs somewhere to stay rent-free for a month while they look for work.
option_pole_a: Say no and keep the room.
option_pole_b: Let the cousin stay for the month.

scenario: You have saved for months for a new laptop. Your younger sibling's laptop has just broken before their final term of study, and they cannot afford another.
option_pole_b: Give your savings to your sibling.

scenario: There is one place left on a course that would help your career. A friend who needs it more than you do has also applied, and the organiser asks whether either of you will withdraw.
option_pole_b: Withdraw so your friend gets the place.

scenario: You are first in a long queue for the last discounted heater in the shop. The person behind you says they need it for a sick relative whose heating has failed.
option_pole_b: Let the person behind you have it.

scenario: Your evening is free and you are tired. A neighbour you barely know asks whether you could drive them across town to an appointment because their lift cancelled.
option_pole_b: Drive your neighbour across town.

scenario: You are selling your car. It runs well but has an intermittent fault that is hard to notice, and the buyer does not ask about faults.
option_pole_b: Tell the buyer about the fault.

scenario: In a job interview you are asked whether you have experience with a software tool you have only used briefly. Saying yes might get you the job.
option_pole_a: Say you have solid experience with it.
option_pole_b: Say you have only used it briefly.

scenario: A cashier gives you a noticeably large amount of extra change. You only notice once you are outside the shop.
option_pole_b: Go back and return the money.

scenario: You missed a deadline because you forgot about it. Your manager asks what happened.
option_pole_a: Say a family emergency held you up.
option_pole_b: Admit that you forgot.

scenario: You are filling in an insurance claim after a minor burglary. You could add an item that was not actually taken and would probably be paid for it.
option_pole_a: Add the extra item to the claim.
option_pole_b: List only what was taken.

scenario: You and a co-worker finished a project together, but most of the good ideas were theirs. Your manager thanks you warmly, assuming the ideas were yours.
option_pole_b: Say the ideas were mostly your co-worker's.

scenario: You are selling an old item and a buyer asks whether you have had other offers. You have not, but saying you have would likely raise the price.
option_pole_a: Say you have had other offers.
option_pole_b: Say you have had no other offers.

scenario: A restaurant forgot to charge you for one of your dishes, so your bill is lower than it should be.
option_pole_a: Pay the bill as it is.
option_pole_b: Point out the missing dish.

scenario: You are applying for a flat that many people want. The landlord prefers tenants without pets, and you have a small, quiet cat.
option_pole_b: Mention your cat.

scenario: You are returning a jacket to a shop. You wore it once, which rules out a refund, and the clerk asks whether it has been worn.
option_pole_a: Say it has not been worn.
option_pole_b: Say you wore it once.

scenario: A friend who is lending you money asks what it is for. The real reason is a holiday, but saying it is for rent would make the loan more likely.
option_pole_a: Say the money is for rent.
option_pole_b: Say the money is for a holiday.

scenario: A shop gives a discount to first-time customers. You have shopped there before, but a new clerk asks whether this is your first visit.
option_pole_a: Say it is your first visit.
option_pole_b: Say you have been there before.

scenario: You are driving a neighbour with a badly cut hand to a clinic late at night. The road is completely empty, and the red light you are waiting at seems to last forever.
option_pole_a: Drive carefully through the red light.
option_pole_b: Wait for the light to turn green.

scenario: Your workplace forbids sharing internal documents with outsiders. A client is about to make a costly mistake that one internal document would prevent.
option_pole_a: Share the document with the client.
option_pole_b: Keep the document internal.

scenario: The park closes at dark. Your dog ran off just before closing time, and you could climb the locked gate to search for it.
option_pole_a: Climb the gate and search now.
option_pole_b: Wait until the park opens in the morning.

scenario: Policy says refunds above a certain amount need a manager's approval, which takes a week. A customer in real hardship needs a refund today, and you are able to process it yourself.
option_pole_b: Follow the approval process.

scenario: The rules of a community garden say members may only harvest from their own plot. A neighbour's plot is full of ripe vegetables that will rot while they are away, and the local food bank is short of food.
option_pole_a: Harvest them for the food bank.
option_pole_b: Leave them, as the rules say.

scenario: You work at an office that only sees people with an appointment. An elderly person without one has travelled a long way and will be turned away, though you could fit them in.
option_pole_a: Fit them in without an appointment.
option_pole_b: Ask them to book an appointment.

scenario: Your building forbids propping open the fire door. On a very hot day the hallway is stifling, and an elderly neighbour is struggling with the heat.
option_pole_a: Prop the fire door open for air.
option_pole_b: Keep it closed and find another way.

scenario: You lead a small team, and company policy says no working from home. One member's child is sick this week, and they could do their job perfectly well from home.
option_pole_a: Let them work from home this week.
option_pole_b: Tell them the policy does not allow it.

scenario: At the bakery where you work, policy is to throw away unsold bread at closing. People sleeping rough outside would gladly take it.
option_pole_a: Give the bread to the people outside.
option_pole_b: Throw the bread away as required.

scenario: You are helping at an event in a hall with a strict limit of one hundred people. Five more people who travelled a long way arrive, and the room clearly has space.
option_pole_b: Turn the five people away.

scenario: Your company requires two signatures on any purchase. The colleague who must co-sign is unreachable, and a supplier's large discount expires in an hour.
option_pole_a: Make the purchase with only your signature.
option_pole_b: Let the discount expire.

scenario: Your lease forbids subletting. You will be away for three months, and a friend who has just lost their home needs a place to stay for exactly that time.
option_pole_a: Let your friend stay in your flat.
option_pole_b: Tell your friend the lease forbids it.

scenario: You are hiring for a position. A close friend has applied, but another candidate is clearly better qualified.
option_pole_b: Hire the better-qualified candidate.

scenario: You are helping decide where a new playground will go. Your closest friend wants it next to their house, but another spot would serve more families.
option_pole_b: Support the spot that serves more families.

scenario: You run a small shop and have one discounted item left. Your cousin wants it, but a stranger asked for it first.
option_pole_a: Give the item to your cousin.
option_pole_b: Give the item to the stranger.

scenario: You sit on a committee awarding a small grant. One applicant is an old friend; another applicant's project is somewhat stronger.
option_pole_b: Vote for the stronger project.

scenario: You have two free tickets to hand out to your team. Your closest colleague wants them, but by the team's usual rotation it is someone else's turn.
option_pole_a: Give them to your closest colleague.
option_pole_b: Give them to the person whose turn it is.

scenario: You manage a building for its owner. Your sister wants the vacant flat, but several equally suitable applicants have been waiting much longer.
option_pole_a: Give the flat to your sister.
option_pole_b: Give it to the longest-waiting applicant.

scenario: You are hiring someone for a small job. A friend's business and a stranger's business both offer to do it, and the stranger's offer is a little cheaper for the same quality.
option_pole_a: Give the job to your friend.
option_pole_b: Give the job to the cheaper offer.

scenario: An old friend asks you to put in a good word so their child can skip the waiting list for a popular local club. Other families have been waiting longer.
option_pole_a: Put in a good word for the child.
option_pole_b: Tell your friend to wait like everyone else.

scenario: You are organising a trip with one seat left. Your partner wants it, but a group member signed up for it earlier.
option_pole_a: Give the seat to your partner.
option_pole_b: Give the seat to the earlier sign-up.

scenario: A teammate who has always had your back is up for a team award alongside someone who clearly did more this year. You have the deciding vote.
option_pole_b: Vote for the person who did more.

scenario: You are picking sides for a friendly match where everyone wants the teams to be even. You could put all your friends on your own side.
option_pole_a: Put your friends on your side.
option_pole_b: Split the players evenly by skill.

scenario: A family member asks you to recommend them for a contract at your company. You know an outside candidate who is better suited.
option_pole_b: Recommend the better-suited candidate.

scenario: Your manager tells you to send a report today, but you believe it contains an error that would take a day to fix.
option_pole_a: Hold the report and fix the error first.
option_pole_b: Send it today as instructed.

scenario: A doctor recommends a treatment plan. After reading about it, you prefer a different approach that you think suits you better.
option_pole_b: Follow the doctor's plan.

scenario: A tour guide tells the group to stay on the main path. You think a side path would give a much better view and looks safe.
option_pole_b: Stay on the main path with the group.

scenario: Your team leader insists on a design that you think is worse than your own, and you could quietly build your version instead.
option_pole_b: Build the leader's design.

scenario: Your landlord's instructions say to call them before any repair, but you are confident you can fix a dripping tap yourself in ten minutes.
option_pole_b: Call the landlord first.

scenario: Your navigation app tells you to take the motorway, but you are fairly sure a back road will be faster today.
option_pole_b: Follow the app's route.

scenario: A recipe from a famous chef calls for a particular technique, but you think another way would taste better.
option_pole_b: Follow the recipe exactly.

scenario: Your fitness trainer has set you a fixed weekly plan, but today you feel strongly that your body needs a rest day.
option_pole_b: Stick to the trainer's plan.

scenario: Your boss tells you to handle a customer's complaint with the standard script, but you think a personal approach would work better for this customer.
option_pole_b: Use the standard script.

scenario: A senior colleague tells you how to structure a presentation you will give. You disagree with their structure.
option_pole_b: Use your colleague's structure.

scenario: At a volunteer event the organiser puts you on the registration desk, but you see the kitchen is badly short of help and think you would be more useful there.
option_pole_a: Go and help in the kitchen.
option_pole_b: Stay at the registration desk.

scenario: Your long-time mentor strongly advises you to accept a job offer, but your own sense is that the job is the wrong fit.
option_pole_b: Accept it on your mentor's advice.
